display.title: The Secret Tunnel
display.summary_short: An aged shamash finally reveals why he polishes the shul's great brass menorah: as a boy, it opened a secret tunnel that saved the whole congregation from armed hooligans.
display.summary_long: A story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast right after Chanukah. Reb Beryl, a shamash of perhaps ninety, keeps the shul spotless because it is Hashem's house, and gives special care to the huge engraved brass menorah beside the Aron HaKodesh. Asked why, he only smiles and says, 'Someday I'll tell you.' At last he shares his secret. When he was young, cruel people tried to stop Jews from learning Torah, and wild hooligans would attack the shul. One day, armed with swords, they surrounded it and gave the worshippers ten minutes to say their last prayers. The rabbi recited Tehillim, then turned one of the menorah's brass arms, opening a secret door to a tunnel that led out of the city. Everyone escaped, and the hooligans, finding the shul empty, fled in fright, crying that it was haunted. The clip continues with a mother's letter about her daughter helping prepare for Shabbos, a lesson that Torah and mitzvos are light showing good from bad, and encouragement for girls to light Shabbos candles.
display.lesson: Hashem saves His people in wondrous ways; treasure and care for the things through which He showed His kindness.
